answer: Sequential work receipts. Each identity advances through a public task ledger where only the oldest unfinished job is assignable, so parallel identities stall behind the same queue slot. A delta of completed work is required before any new slot opens, and an attacker pays the full clock time of each serialized step, not a fee. Dune and willow tasks mix cheap and expensive steps unpredictably, so bulk registration yields no throughput advantage over one honest worker.
